skill.description: Deploy Flask, Django, and FastAPI projects to Azure App Service Linux using Azure CLI or Azure Developer CLI guidance.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are benign Azure CLI documentation examples, placeholder URLs, 0.0.0.0 bind addresses, relative documentation links, or .env exclusions. The executable retry wrappers contain a real command-injection risk because they accept full command strings and execute them dynamically. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Retry wrappers execute full command strings dynamically.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval and powershell -Command string execution with fixed functions or argument arrays. Validate app, resource group, plan, and region values before invoking Azure CLI.

remediation.issue: User-supplied Azure resource values can be used verbatim in commands.
remediation.suggestion: Document strict allowed characters for resource names and quote every argument. Reject values containing shell metacharacters before calling helper scripts.

content.user_title: Deploy Python Apps to Azure App Service
content.value_statement: Python teams need repeatable App Service deployments without guessing Azure CLI steps. This skill guides creation, configuration, deployment, and final user messaging for Flask, Django, and FastAPI apps.
actual_capabilities: Detects Flask, Django, FastAPI, generic WSGI, ASGI, and unknown Python projects.
Guides idempotent creation of resource groups, Linux App Service plans, and web apps.
Chooses Azure Developer CLI deployment when azure.yaml targets App Service.
Sets server-side build configuration and FastAPI startup commands.
Packages and deploys code with Azure CLI zip deployment guidance.
Returns the App Service URL and log guidance without premature health probes.
limitations: Does not deploy Container Apps, Azure Functions, AKS, or custom containers.
Does not create databases, Key Vault, VNet integration, or IaC-managed environments.
Requires an authenticated Azure CLI or Azure Developer CLI with sufficient permissions.
Bundled retry wrappers execute command strings and need sanitized resource values.

use_cases.title: First App Service Deploy
use_cases.description: Deploy a small Flask, Django, or FastAPI app to Linux App Service with generated resource names.

use_cases.title: Repeatable Team Deployment
use_cases.description: Apply consistent Azure CLI steps for resource creation, startup configuration, and zip deployment.

use_cases.title: Azd App Service Release
use_cases.description: Use an existing azure.yaml App Service project and deploy through Azure Developer CLI.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy My Python App
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this Python web app to Azure App Service Linux. Ask only for the app name if needed, then use safe defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy With Existing Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this FastAPI app to App Service using my existing resource group, plan, region, and subscription values.

prompt_templates.title: Review Startup Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect the framework in this project and configure the App Service startup behavior before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Transient Azure Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this app and apply the transient Azure create retry guidance only if resource creation fails with retryable errors.

output_examples.input: Deploy my Flask app with a generated name.
output_examples.output: Reports the detected Flask project, creates the Azure resources, deploys the zip package, and returns the App Service URL.

output_examples.input: Deploy this FastAPI project to my existing resource group.
output_examples.output: Uses the provided Azure resources, sets the uvicorn startup command, enables server-side build, and prints the deployment message.

output_examples.input: This project has azure.yaml for App Service.
output_examples.output: Chooses the Azure Developer CLI path, deploys the service, and returns the endpoint without probing the site.

best_practices: Confirm the target subscription and region before creating Azure resources.
Keep requirements.txt or pyproject.toml accurate so App Service can build dependencies.
Validate resource names before passing them into shell or PowerShell commands.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for Container Apps, Functions, AKS, or full infrastructure planning.
Do not run early HTTP probes and treat warm-up errors as deployment failure.
Do not pass unsanitized user strings into the bundled retry wrapper scripts.

faq.question: Which Python frameworks does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Flask, Django, FastAPI, and generic Python web apps with manual startup guidance.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide creation of a resource group, Linux App Service plan, and web app when missing.

faq.question: Can it use Azure Developer CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses azd when azure.yaml exists and targets App Service.

faq.question: Does it verify the deployed site?
faq.answer: No. It avoids immediate probes because App Service can need several minutes to warm up.

faq.question: Does it manage databases or private networking?
faq.answer: No. It hands off those broader infrastructure needs to a preparation workflow.

faq.question: What security review result matters most?
faq.answer: The retry wrapper scripts need safer command execution before broad marketplace publication.
